title: Akamai Q3 2026 earnings scorecard
status: Pre-release — Q3 results are not yet published
purpose: Turn the next Akamai earnings release into a repeatable company-capture test. This scorecard compares reported facts with company-issued guidance and the Q2 baseline; it does not create a forecast, target price, or expectation-gap conclusion.

event.timing: Exact reporting date is pending Akamai's announcement. The company says Q3 results are usually reported near the beginning of November.

reportedBaseline.label: Q2 CIS revenue
reportedBaseline.note: Fast-growing but still a small portion of total revenue

reportedBaseline.label: Q2 security / delivery mix
reportedBaseline.note: Security growth must offset legacy delivery pressure

reportedBaseline.label: Q2 CIS commitments
reportedBaseline.note: Includes a >$600M four-year robotics-related contract; commitments are not revenue

checks.title: Deliver the guide before interpreting the mix
checks.question: Did reported Q3 revenue, non-GAAP operating margin, and EPS land within or above the company-issued ranges?
checks.baseline: Q3 guidance: revenue $1.105–$1.130B, non-GAAP operating margin 24%–26%, and non-GAAP EPS $1.60–$1.80.
checks.upgrade: Results meet or exceed the stated ranges, and management maintains or improves the full-year outlook without relying on an unexplained one-off.
checks.notEnough: A guide beat alone establishes execution, not agentic capture or durable economics.
checks.downgrade: Results miss the low end, or guidance is reduced because demand, fulfillment, pricing, or capacity economics deteriorated.
checks.decisionImpact: A clean guide result keeps the capture test open; a miss strengthens the no-meaningful-Wave-2 path.

checks.title: Convert CIS commitments into revenue quality
checks.question: Did CIS revenue remain strong, and did management disclose evidence that signed commitments are converting into revenue, backlog, usage, or a credible deployment schedule?
checks.baseline: Q2 CIS revenue was $99M, up 39% year over year; year-to-date CIS commitments exceeded $2.8B.
checks.upgrade: CIS growth remains strong and management ties a material portion of commitments to deployment, recognized revenue, recurring usage, or visible backlog conversion.
checks.notEnough: Another large contract or a generic pipeline statement without timing, conversion, customer concentration, or economics.
checks.downgrade: CIS growth slows sharply, commitments fail to turn into reported activity, or delivery timelines and hardware availability push conversion outward.
checks.decisionImpact: Only conversion evidence can begin to support the material-Wave-2 scenario’s revenue bridge.

checks.title: Show paid agent-control monetization
checks.question: Did Akamai quantify revenue, customer adoption, attach, price realization, retention, or usage for Bot & Agent Control, AI fetcher controls, inference, or another named agent-related product?
checks.baseline: Akamai has separated AI fetchers and agents in its controls, but it has not disclosed agent-specific revenue, pricing, or attach rate.
checks.upgrade: Management names a paid product, customer count, attach, revenue contribution, or pricing mechanism linked to agentic workloads or controls.
checks.notEnough: A new product feature, taxonomy, security report, or customer anecdote with no commercial metric.
checks.downgrade: Management confirms the controls are bundled, free, or nonmaterial, or offers no commercial signal while claiming product relevance.
checks.decisionImpact: Without a paid mechanism, agentic traffic remains an infrastructure narrative rather than shareholder-capture evidence.

checks.title: Contain the legacy delivery drag
checks.question: Did delivery and other cloud applications stabilize, or was its decline more than offset by durable, appropriately profitable security and CIS growth?
checks.baseline: Q2 delivery and other cloud applications revenue was $396M, down 6% year over year; security revenue was $604M, up 10%.
checks.upgrade: Delivery trends improve, or the company demonstrates that mix shift toward security and CIS improves growth quality without sacrificing returns.
checks.notEnough: A fast-growing CIS category while the larger delivery base continues to deteriorate and masks total-company economics.
checks.downgrade: Delivery weakness broadens through pricing pressure, traffic optimization, renewals, or customer cost control and offsets the higher-growth categories.
checks.decisionImpact: A durable mix shift is necessary before treating CIS growth as a whole-company rerating engine.

checks.title: Prove capacity investment earns a cash return
checks.question: Did reported operating margin, cash from operations, capital investment, and management commentary show that cloud and AI capacity spending is becoming productive rather than simply larger?
checks.baseline: Q2 non-GAAP operating margin was 25%, down five points year over year; Q2 cash from operations was $326M. The 10-Q flags rising server, memory, co-location, bandwidth, depreciation, and related capacity costs.
checks.upgrade: Margins remain within or above guide while cash generation and disclosed capital investment support a credible improving return path.
checks.notEnough: Revenue growth without enough information on capex, hosting costs, depreciation, gross margin, or cash conversion.
checks.downgrade: Margin falls below guide, cash conversion weakens, or management raises spending needs without showing conversion, pricing, or return evidence.
checks.decisionImpact: This is the critical bridge between a demand signal and the scenario lab’s free-cash-flow assumptions.

checks.title: Interrogate concentration and fulfillment risk
checks.question: Did the large CIS contracts create dependency, timing risk, capacity constraints, or customer-specific economics that weaken the quality of the reported growth?
checks.baseline: The disclosed greater-than-$600M robotics-related contract runs over four years; Akamai identifies fulfillment, procurement, and projected-capex risk in its filings.
checks.upgrade: Management explains deployment timing, diversification, capacity readiness, and contract economics without revealing an adverse concentration or fulfillment dependency.
checks.notEnough: A larger commitment headline with no information about timing, service obligations, concentration, or cash needs.
checks.downgrade: Customer delay, cancellation, concentration, hardware constraint, or contract economics indicate the commitment is less valuable or more capital-intensive than implied.
checks.decisionImpact: Large commitments count only after their economics and execution risks are visible.

postReleaseProtocol: Capture results, guidance, and management commentary as company-reported facts with the earnings-release and filing links.
Append the Q3 record to data/manual/company-capture-history.json before replacing the current AKAM card baseline.
Mark each scorecard line as observed, unresolved, or contrary. Do not use a single green line to override a contrary margin, cash, or delivery result.
Revise the Akamai scenario assumptions only if reported conversion, monetization, and cash-return evidence supports a changed economic path.
Keep Gap Readiness separate: a Q3 result can improve company capture, but cannot establish an expectation gap without aligned consensus-revision and valuation history.

decisionRules.definition: Guide execution plus visible CIS conversion and no material worsening in delivery, margin, or cash-return evidence. A disclosed paid agent-control mechanism would strengthen the result.
decisionRules.action: Advance AKAM to a two-period company-capture review; do not call an expectation gap yet.

decisionRules.definition: Guide execution or CIS growth is present, but commercial agent evidence, conversion timing, or return on capacity remains unresolved.
decisionRules.action: Keep the existing early-capture state and preserve the counterarguments.

decisionRules.definition: Guide miss, commitment conversion delay, worsening delivery drag, or capacity economics materially weaken the route to durable free cash flow.
decisionRules.action: Move probability weight toward the no-meaningful-Wave-2 scenario and record the breaker.
